sn42.5:1.2: “Sir, I have heard this said by the cavalrymen of the past, the tutors of tutors:
sn42.5:1.3: ‘When a cavalryman strives and struggles in battle, and the enemy strike him down and finish him off, then when his body breaks up, after death, he is reborn in the company of the defeated gods.’
sn42.5:1.4: What does the Buddha say about this?”
sn42.5:1.5: “Enough, chief, let it be. Don’t ask me about that.”
sn42.5:2.2: And for a third time the cavalry chief said to the Buddha:
sn42.5:2.3: “Sir, I have heard this said by the cavalrymen of the past, the tutors of tutors:
sn42.5:2.4: ‘When a cavalryman strives and struggles in battle, and the enemy strike him down and finish him off, then when his body breaks up, after death, he is reborn in the company of the defeated gods.’
sn42.5:2.5: What does the Buddha say about this?”
sn42.5:3.1: “Clearly, chief, I can’t get you to accept it when I say:
sn42.5:3.2: ‘Enough, chief, let it be. Don’t ask me about that.’
sn42.5:3.3: Still, I will explain it to you.
sn42.5:3.4: When a cavalryman strives and struggles in battle, the mind he has taken up beforehand is badly made and badly directed:
sn42.5:3.5: ‘May these sentient beings be killed, or bound, or cut off, or destroyed, or may they cease to exist!’
sn42.5:3.6: As he strives and struggles, the enemy strike him down and finish him off, and when his body breaks up, after death, he is reborn in the hell called the Defeated.
sn42.5:3.7: But if he holds a view like this:
sn42.5:3.8: ‘When a cavalryman strives and struggles in battle, and the enemy strike him down and finish him off, then when his body breaks up, after death, he is reborn in the company of the defeated gods.’ That is his wrong view.
sn42.5:3.9: For a person with wrong view, chief, I say there is one of two destinations—
sn42.5:4.1: When this was said, the cavalry chief wept and let his tears flow.
sn42.5:4.2: “This is what I couldn’t get you to accept, chief, when I said:
sn42.5:4.3: ‘Enough, chief, let it be. Don’t ask me about that.’”
sn42.5:4.4: “Sir, I’m not crying because of what the Buddha has said to me.
sn42.5:4.5: But for a long time, sir, I have been cheated, deceived, and enticed by the cavalrymen of the past, the tutors of tutors, who said:
sn42.5:4.6: ‘When a cavalryman strives and struggles in battle, and the enemy strike him down and finish him off, then when his body breaks up, after death, he is reborn in the company of the defeated gods.’”
